reader_summary.headline: This is the memo by Howard Marks, The Illusion of Knowledge.
reader_summary.overview: This is the memo by Howard Marks, The Illusion of Knowledge. I've been expressing my disregard for forecasts for almost as long as I've been writing my memos, starting with the value of predictions. Over the years since then, I've explained at length why I'm not interested in forecasts.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that macroeconomic forecasts are futile because the complexity of human behavior, psychological factors, and unpredictable events like pandemics make it impossible to build a reliable model of an economy. He concludes that the greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, but the illusion of knowledge, as past statistical patterns cannot reliably predict future economic outcomes due to a lack of stationarity.
